ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening applies to all directors, ultimate beneficial owners, authorised signatories, and material counterparties. Use at least three independent sources: (i) OFAC SDN and Sectoral Sanctions Identifications List; (ii) United Nations Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List; (iii) New Zealand sanctions lists administered by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade under the New Zealand Sanctions Act 2020; plus (iv) domestic AML databases supervised by the Department of Internal Affairs. Politically Exposed Persons require enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth verification, beneficial-interest tracing, and escalation to senior management. Screening must cover name aliases and fuzzy matching, be re-run on a continuous basis, and be documented in the company AML/CFT compliance file.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Register, Companies Office (companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names must use Latin script (English transliteration) for the registered name; non-English script can be included only after the English transliteration has been approved. The Companies Office applies the Companies Act 1993 name availability rules and guidelines, including the four-stage assessment: (1) identity with existing names; (2) restricted and sensitive words; (3) likelihood of misleading the public; and (4) public interest and objectionable-name review. Diacritics are preserved for Te Reo Maori vocabulary, but a common English form or phonetic transliteration is required, and the Registrar may require removal or variation of any name that is not capable of clear verbal translation or accurate records.

stage_1.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant will receive the Companies Office decision with a reason code. The applicant may file a request for reconsideration with the Senior Registrar of Companies within 20 working days of notice, explaining why the name is not identical, misleading, or objectionable, and submitting fresh availability results. The Registrar must issue a written decision. If reconsideration is unsuccessful, the applicant may appeal by urgent application to the High Court under the Companies Act 1993 and the Judicial Review Procedure Act 2016, or apply for a new name reservation with corrected tokens. A separate objection to a conflicting reserved name may be lodged by interested parties.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (Public Act 1993 No 105), including, among others, sections 12 and 14 on incorporation and certificate of incorporation, section 17 on the constitution, section 87 on share certificates, section 122 on the registered office, and section 160 on appointment of directors.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), Wellington, online register at register.companiesoffice.govt.nz
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Company under section 12 of the Companies Act 1993, filed electronically through the New Zealand Companies Register, together with the constitution, director and shareholder consents, and prescribed fee.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required under the Companies Act 1993. The company must issue at least one share but there is no blocked escrow deposit requirement. Shares may be paid in money or other lawful consideration if the board determines the consideration is adequate; no minimum capital needs to be held in a blocked bank account. Non-resident ownership is permitted.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME], a limited company incorporated under the Companies Act 1993 of New Zealand. RESOLVED, that the following resolutions are hereby adopted at a duly convened meeting of the board of directors of the Company, at which a quorum of directors was present throughout and that the board minutes be recorded as follows. 1. Share Capital Subscription. RESOLVED that the initial issued share capital of the Company be and is hereby approved and recorded as [NUMBER] ordinary shares of no par value, with the rights and restrictions set out in the Company's constitution, and that the board authorizes the allotment, issue, and registration of those shares to the initial subscribers whose names and addresses appear in the application for incorporation. RESOLVED FURTHER that share certificates are approved, that the share register is to be maintained at the registered office, and that the subscription consideration is recorded as fully or partly paid as disclosed to the Registrar. 2. Banking Authorization. RESOLVED that the Company shall open and maintain a corporate bank account with a licensed bank in New Zealand for the purpose of receiving SWIFT wire transfers and conducting wire transfer payments. RESOLVED FURTHER that the directors and the company secretary, if appointed, are authorized to negotiate account terms, sign account opening documents, execute banking mandates, and designate authorized signatories, with any payment exceeding NZD 10,000 to require a dual approval unless the board resolves otherwise. 3. Registered Office and Address for Service. RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company be fixed at [REGISTERED OFFICE ADDRESS], New Zealand, and that the address for service is [ADDRESS FOR SERVICE]. RESOLVED FURTHER that the Company keep the register of shareholders, directors, and other statutory records at that address, and that any future change of registered office or address for service be filed with the Registrar of Companies as required under the Companies Act 1993. 4. Appointment of Statutory Officers. RESOLVED that [DIRECTOR NAME] be and is hereby appointed as director and managing director, that [OTHER DIRECTOR NAME] be and is hereby appointed as director, and that [SECRETARY NAME] be and is hereby appointed as company secretary, each to act until a successor is elected or appointed. RESOLVED FURTHER that the board confirms that the Company has at least one director ordinarily resident in New Zealand, and each appointee has accepted office with a signed consent. 5. General Authority. RESOLVED that any director or the company secretary is authorized, acting singly, to execute all applications, declarations, notices, and registrations required to give effect to this resolution, to instruct the bank, and to do all acts necessary to commence lawful business, and that this resolution be lodged with the bank, the Registrar, and other parties as appropriate. Certified as a true and correct minute of the board meeting. Dated [DATE]. Chairman of the Board.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company name availability check and name reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office via the Companies Register online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Check the proposed company name against the New Zealand Companies Register using the name availability search tool in the online portal. Submit a name reservation application to hold an approved name for the statutory period, then verify that at least one proposed director is an individual ordinarily resident in New Zealand or otherwise permitted to act under the Companies Act 1993. Collect signed consents to act from all directors and shareholders, confirm the registered office will be physically located in New Zealand, and prepare the constitutional documentation, including any permitted limitations on company purpose and share transfer provisions.
required_dossiers: Reserved company name certificate or name availability reference
Full legal names, residential addresses, and dates of birth of all proposed directors
Consent to act of each director
Proposed registered office physical address in New Zealand
Constitutional draft or election to rely on the statutory default rules
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or suspended, the Companies Office will identify the conflicting name; the applicant may submit a substituted name within 10 business days or request reconsideration with supporting distinctiveness evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and electronic lodgement of incorporation application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Registration Operations Unit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the Companies Office online application for registration of a company under section 12 of the Companies Act 1993. Enter the reserved company name, the proposed address of the registered office and address for service, the full legal names and residential addresses of all shareholders and directors, and the class and amounts of shares. Attach the signed constitution or elect to adopt the default rules in Schedule 1. Upload the consent forms and identity documents for each officer, declare any ordinary residential information required by the Registrar, and pay the prescribed registration fee through the online payment gateway. Any documents executed overseas must be notarized and, where required, apostilled before upload. After submission, monitor the Companies Register dashboard for any completeness query.
required_dossiers: Completed incorporation application form
Company constitution or written election to adopt the default constitution in Schedule 1
Signed consent to act of each director and shareholder
Certified passport or national identity document for each director and shareholder
Proof of residential address for overseas directors and shareholders
Shareholder subscription schedule with class and number of shares
Payment confirmation for the registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried for incomplete information, correct and resubmit the deficient particulars within 15 business days. If suspension occurs due to unpaid fees, pay the outstanding amount within five business days. If the application is rejected, file a fresh incorporation application using the reserved name if it remains available and attach any corrective notices requested by the Registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of certificate of incorporation and company register extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the Company Overview dashboard through the Companies Register using the RealMe login to retrieve the Certificate of Incorporation and the New Zealand Business Number generated upon approval. Review the registered particulars to ensure the directors and shareholder details, company name, and registered office are correctly recorded. Download the certificate as a PDF and print an official company extract or statement of registered particulars, where available, for use in bank account opening and contractual counterparty due diligence. The company comes into existence only upon the issue of the certificate in accordance with section 14 of the Companies Act 1993. Confirm that the certificate date is the effective incorporation date and that no conditions have been attached.
required_dossiers: Approved incorporation application reference
Company name and identification code
RealMe login credentials for the Companies Register
Certificate of Incorporation in downloadable PDF form
Companies Register company extract for record-keeping
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is not automatically generated after approval, contact the Companies Office online help desk with the application reference. If any registered particular contains a typographical or legal error, request a correction through an online notice of change of particulars; no substantive business is to be transacted before the certificate is available.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of corporate bank account and activation of SWIFT wire capability
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed New Zealand trading bank selected by the board
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the Certificate of Incorporation, the pro-forma board resolution authorizing bank account opening, and the company constitution to a licensed New Zealand trading bank. Complete the bank's account opening application, including the business activity description for ISIC 7490 trade-remedy defense consulting, the expected monthly transaction value and source of funds, the ownership chain and beneficial ownership schedule, and the purpose of SWIFT wire transfer usage. Provide each intended signatory's certified passport and proof of residence, and execute the bank's facility terms. The bank will complete an anti-money laundering and countering financing of terrorism review under New Zealand's Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 before activating the operating account.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Constitution and board banking resolution
Beneficial ownership schedule and shareholder register
Certified passport and proof of address for all directors and signatories
Business activity description for ISIC 7490
Expected transaction volumes and source of funds statement
Board resolution designating signatories and two-signatory threshold
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires additional beneficial ownership detail, supply an updated ownership schedule within five business days. If the bank declines the application, convene a board resolution to select an alternate licensed bank and complete enhanced due diligence forms where needed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inland Revenue registration and statutory tax profile setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), New Zealand, via myIR Services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the incorporated company for an IRD number through Inland Revenue's myIR portal or by filing Form IR596, using the NZBN and registered office address. Complete the Goods and Services Tax registration application if the company expects taxable supplies to exceed NZD 60,000 within a 12-month period, or elect to register voluntarily if the business is to claim input credits on professional fees. Provide directors' identification and the actual business activity classification code, ISIC 7490, ensure all future operating income will be appropriately traced, and set up the payment frequency for provisional tax and any employer obligations.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
New Zealand Business Number
Company constitution and registered office address
Directors' identification documents
Business activity description using ISIC 7490
Corporate bank account details for refund and direct debit purposes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If IRD issues a completeness notice, respond through myIR within 10 business days with certified identification and proof of address. If the IRD number is delayed, continue the payroll or invoicing timetable using alternative compliant procedures and apply for late payment penalty remission if the delay was caused by IRD processing.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - the ISIC 7490 trade-remedy defense consulting business is a professional digital and advisory service without physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing operations in ISIC categories 1xxx, 2xxx, 3xxx, 4xxx or 52xx. For reserved legal or accounting services, the relevant regulators are the New Zealand Law Society and Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no industrial operating permit, factory license, manufacturing license, assembly permit, warehouse permit, or building occupation certificate is required for the principal consulting activity. If reserved legal work is provided, the individual lawyer must hold a current practising certificate under the Lawyers and Conveyancers Act 2006; if reserved accounting work is provided, the individual accountant must hold membership and a practising certificate from Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority New Zealand (Not Applicable for this service activity)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no Environmental Impact Assessment, resource consent, or environmental registration is triggered by office-based trade-remedy defense consulting under ISIC 7490. An EIA could become necessary only if the company later establishes physical manufacturing or warehousing activity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - no wastewater discharge, volatile organic compound emissions, or hazardous waste streams are generated by this professional service. If future operations add physical premises or industrial processes, the company must comply with the Resource Management Act 1991, applicable regional and district plan limits, and National Environmental Standards for air quality, water quality, and hazardous substances.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for pure consulting because no civil defense fire certificate, structural load inspection, or industrial safety approval is required. Any leased professional office must nevertheless comply with the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015, the Building Act 2004, and local authority fire safety requirements, including safe means of egress, working smoke detection, and electrical appliance testing.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) – online portal: myIR (https://www.ird.govt.nz/myir)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For foreign non-resident entities not incorporated in New Zealand, the IRD number is the statutory tax identification number. The procedure is: (1) determine whether the entity is carrying on a taxable activity in New Zealand or has any New Zealand-source income; (2) prepare certified copies of the foreign certificate of incorporation, constitutional documents, board resolution authorising the New Zealand application, register of shareholders and directors, and proof of overseas tax residence; (3) file the Inland Revenue application for a non-resident company IRD number through myIR or the Inland Revenue contact centre; (4) appoint a New Zealand address for service and, where required, a tax agent; (5) upon issue, use the IRD number for all tax filings and assessments; (6) if taxable supplies exceed or are expected to exceed NZD 60,000 in any 12-month period, register for GST in myIR within 21 days after the obligation arises, with the IRD number serving as the GST registration number. If the entity will not carry on a taxable activity but has withholding obligations, it must still notify Inland Revenue for registration of the appropriate withholding tax account type.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None – New Zealand does not provide a check-the-box election or any elective entity-classification regime. Hybrid mismatch arrangements are addressed under the Taxation (Neutralising Business Hybrids) Act 2018; no elective framework exists for entity-level tax status.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 in taxable supplies in any 12-month period, actual or expected
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, no API stamping requirement, and no anti-fraud digital stamping regime applies to GST invoices in New Zealand. Registered persons must issue tax invoices containing the prescribed particulars, and must provide a tax invoice within 28 days of a request from the recipient. The voluntary Peppol e-invoicing framework is supported for B2B electronic exchange, but Inland Revenue does not operate a real-time clearance or pre-clearance approval system for standard GST invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under section 11 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, supplies of goods are zero-rated when the supplier exports the goods from New Zealand within 28 days of the time of supply, or when the goods are placed in New Zealand and the supplier is satisfied that the non-resident recipient will export them within that statutory period. Qualifying services, including legal and trade-defense consulting services for international anti-dumping inquiries, are zero-rated when supplied to a non-resident recipient who is outside New Zealand at the time the services are performed, provided the services are not supplied in connection with land or goods in New Zealand and do not fall within any statutory excepted supply. Digital services supplied to New Zealand consumers remain subject to GST; however, a New Zealand supplier may zero-rate qualifying services supplied to non-resident recipients who are outside New Zealand upon retention of adequate evidence of the recipient's non-resident status.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Entry lodged via the New Zealand Customs Service Trade Single Window)
Bill of Lading for sea freight or Air Waybill for air freight evidencing physical departure from New Zealand
Commercial invoice and packing list describing the exported goods or services
Bank or foreign exchange remittance records, including SWIFT confirmations, evidencing settlement of the export invoice in foreign currency
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue may audit export zero-rating claims and require proof that goods were physically exported within 28 days or that the services recipient was a non-resident outside New Zealand. If the supporting documentation is not substantiated, the zero rating is retrospectively reversed and GST at the standard 15% rate is reassessed from the time of supply, with late payment penalties and use-of-money interest under the Tax Administration Act 1994. Abusive tax positions can attract a 100% shortfall penalty, and fraudulent GST evasion is a criminal offence. Additionally, false export declarations may trigger penalties imposed by the New Zealand Customs Service under the Customs and Excise Act 2018. The 180-day benchmark in this dossier reflects the standard administrative expectation for assembling and preserving export-settlement documentation; New Zealand does not impose a separate statutory FX repatriation deadline for GST zero-rating purposes.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand maintains an open capital and current account regime without foreign exchange controls. The Reserve Bank of New Zealand supervises banks and promotes a sound financial system, but it does not approve or block ordinary cross-border transfers. New Zealand dollars are freely convertible into major international currencies onshore and offshore. Non-residents may own 100% of a New Zealand limited company, appoint directors, and hold funds in domestic or foreign currency accounts. Export proceeds are fully retainable, and there is no requirement to convert foreign currency into NZD. Inward capital injections are permitted without prior RBNZ approval, subject to standard bank know-your-customer, anti-money-laundering and sanctions screening. The Overseas Investment Act may apply only if the entity acquires sensitive land or significant business assets, which is not relevant for ISIC 7490 professional anti-dumping defense services. Profit repatriation is subject to normal tax administration: dividends paid to non-resident shareholders attract non-resident withholding tax at applicable treaty rates, and the company must satisfy imputation ratio requirements. There are no surrender requirements, no exchange approval certificates needed, and no separate capital control registry. The main practical hurdles are documentary, not regulatory: banks require source-of-wealth evidence, beneficial ownership declarations, and board resolutions, particularly for large lump-sum fee payments. Overall, New Zealand's regulatory environment offers low currency convertibility friction and a highly reliable multilateral clearing and SWIFT infrastructure.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender requirement exists in New Zealand. Exporters may retain 100% of foreign currency receipts indefinitely in either New Zealand dollar or foreign currency accounts. There is no mandatory conversion ratio, no conversion window, and no central bank directive requiring repatriation; banks only submit balance-of-payments statistical reports to the Reserve Bank of New Zealand.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational NZD and USD Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational NZD and USD Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational NZD and USD Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Strong ancillary viability but not primary. Because New Zealand has no exchange controls, licensed non-bank electronic money institutions such as Wise and Airwallex can legally onboard the New Zealand entity, hold NZD and multi-currency balances, and support cross-border fee collections for trade defense services. However, these EMIs are not registered banks under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act and cannot provide access to the local ESAS clearing system, direct debit facilities, documentary letters of credit, or committed overdraft liquidity. For anti-dumping defense work receiving funds from government agencies and corporate counterparties, an EMI can be used for low-risk collections and disbursements after completing EMI KYC, but the primary treasury relationship must remain with a tier-1 commercial bank to ensure full clearing rails, sanctions screening accountability, and robust capital verification.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical in-branch appearance is generally not mandatory for standard-risk corporate clients in New Zealand. The major tier-1 banks permit remote onboarding using secure video interviews with statutory directors and beneficial owners, combined with certified copies of passports, proof of residential address, and a New Zealand registered office confirmation. Remote consular proxy opening is not a standard alternative; instead, offshore directors are expected to complete an electronic identity verification call or attend via bank-approved video conference. The bank will normally require the company secretary or a New Zealand-based director to coordinate the appointment and provide certified corporate documents from the Companies Office within 30 days of opening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex offshore ownership with a discretionary trust or nominee shareholder obscuring underlying beneficial ownership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the trust deed, a registered person of significant control (PSC) extract from the New Zealand Companies Office, a group structure chart showing all layers, directors' and settlors' passports, and an independent legal opinion confirming the ultimate beneficial owner identification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Counterparty fund flows originating from anti-dumping respondents or government authorities in high-risk or sanctioned trade jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed KYC pack for each client counterparty, signed trade-defense engagement letter, official anti-dumping proceeding docket or case reference, commercial invoices or fee schedule, bank account details of each payer, sanctions screening output, and a written attestation that services are legal defense and not export-controlled technology.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large lump-sum professional fee payments received through intermediary law or consulting firms without clear matter linkage.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Matter-specific fee agreement, itemized bill of services with hours and expenses, court or investigating authority filing stamps, underlying customs questionnaires, and ledger extracts from the referring firm confirming the exact matter reference and source of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital injection from directors without verifiable source of wealth, especially in jurisdictions with tax-haven features.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve months of personal bank statements, tax residence certificates, income tax returns, dividend declarations, share sale agreements, statutory declaration of source of wealth, and a notarized accountant confirmation.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Remit through SWIFT MT103 in USD or NZD to the company's tier-1 bank account. Use the purpose code 'Capital contribution / equity injection' as mapped by the receiving bank; include the New Zealand company name and registration number in the remittance information. No RBNZ prior approval is required. For capital verification retain the SWIFT MT103 confirmation, the director resolution approving the injection, updated share register, Companies Office extract, and the bank's inward credit advice. If the capitalization involves foreign trust funds, include the trust deed and trustee resolution.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SWIFT MT103/MT202 for direct fee payments to overseas anti-dumping counsel; SWIFT MT700 documentary letters of credit for trade-adjacent settlements; documentary collections (D/P and D/A) for goods-related transactions; and New Zealand domestic payments through the ESAS high-value system or Direct Debit rails for local disbursements. All outbound payments are subject to sanctions screening, transaction monitoring, and bank-mandated source-of-funds documentation for unusual amounts.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: NZD/USD spot and deliverable FX forwards for documented legal fee or tax cash flows
NZD cross-currency swaps for the full term of any material foreign-currency borrowing
Vanilla FX options to hedge unfunded contingencies in anti-dumping case costs

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not generally permitted onshore because NZD is fully deliverable; offshore NDFs are acceptable only where a bank is unable to deliver NZD, and only with genuine economic exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Companies Act 1993 Annual Return (Confirmation of Shareholding, Directors and Registered Particulars)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Deliver within the window from 28 days before to 30 days after the company return date (incorporation anniversary or the elected return date); online filing via the Companies Office register; non-filing immediately attracts reminders and late fee escalation.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional NZ $65 (USD $40) late filing fee; failure to file for two consecutive years triggers the s 318 removal procedure with 20-working-day notice and administrative strike-off; directors may incur personal liability for debts incurred while trading during removal.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Company Income Tax Return (IR4) and Related Attachments
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Standard 31 March balance date: self-filed companies due 7 July; tax-agent clients due 31 March of the following year. Non-standard balance date: due on the last day of the 7th month after balance date (tax-agent schedule available).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure-to-file penalty NZ $50 plus NZ $50 per month up to NZ $500; late payment penalty of 1% on the first day, additional 4% on the 7th day, then 1% per month; Use-of-Money Interest (UOMI) accrues on all unpaid tax at the IRD prescribed payer rate.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Fringe Benefit Tax Annual Return (IR 425) if the company provides non-cash fringe benefits to employees
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Final annual return for the 31 March FBT year due 30 April; quarterly filers lodge by the 20th of the month following each quarter end; payday filers use the IRD prescribed schedule.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty NZ $50 per month up to NZ $500; late payment penalties of 1% / 4% / monthly 1% as for income tax; UOMI applies to unpaid FBT from the due date; materially late filings may trigger IRD default assessments.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A compulsory independent audit applies to (i) FMC reporting entities under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013; (ii) non-FMC companies that are 25% or more overseas-owned with total assets or total revenue above NZ $10 million (audited financial statements must be filed with the Companies Office); and (iii) any company where shareholders holding at least 5% of voting rights validly require an audit under s 202 Companies Act 1993. An ordinary private consultancy below the NZ $60 million asset / NZ $30 million revenue 'large' thresholds is audit-exempt unless a shareholder or the constitution requires otherwise.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand equivalents to IFRS (NZ IFRS) with the Reduced Disclosure Regime permitted for Tier 2 non-reporting entities; small companies may adopt the New Zealand Simple Format Reporting (NZ SFR) standard; income tax calculations follow the Income Tax Act 2007 and Tax Administration Act 1994.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand does not operate a standalone UBO filing. The Companies Office annual return records the full share register, directors, and any ultimate holding company holding 25% or more of shares. Independently, the company as an AML/CFT reporting entity supervised by the Department of Internal Affairs must conduct ongoing due diligence on business relationships and re-identify beneficial owners whenever a trust, corporate transaction, or a 25% or greater ownership change occurs.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (ss 87-89 Companies Act 1993, including share transfers and holdings)
Minute Book for directors' and shareholders' meetings and resolutions (s 189 Companies Act 1993)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 60-500 per annum (NZD 100-800) for registered office service and corporate secretarial management, depending on whether the agent also prepares the annual return, minutes, and Companies Office filings
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000-18,500 (NZD 10,000-30,000) for an annual independent audit of a small-to-mid-sized trade-defense consultancy, subject to transaction volume, related-party confirmations, and cross-border evidence procedures

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Standard 28% headline rate applies to the NZ Ltd engaged in ISIC 7490 anti-dumping trade defense consulting. No industry-specific tax holiday exists in New Zealand. Preferential features: full imputation credit system eliminating economic double taxation on dividends; R&D Tax Incentive of 15% on eligible R&D expenditure; immediate expensing of low-value assets up to NZ$5,000; full deductibility of ordinary professional wages, expert witness fees, and trade-remedy compliance costs; zero-rated GST treatment for exported consulting services to non-residents.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite (no statutory 5-year cap under Income Tax Act 2007 s IA 4; continuity of shareholding of at least 49% or business continuity/same-business test required to preserve losses)
